newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's April 15 budget-summary of media reports.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's April 15 budget-summary of media reports.

text.p: Following is a summary of what the Swedish media has reported on the likely contents of the minority Social Democratic government's April 15 budget proposal.
This summary will be repeated daily ahead of the budget and new or expanded items will be marked with an asterisk *.
-- Forecast for the 1998 budget surplus raised to 12 billion crowns from 10 billion crowns.

-- Municipalities to get six billion crowns and regional authorities two billion of the 10 billion crowns that Prime Minister Goran Persson has promised annually in extra measures for health, care of the elderly and schools.
-- Early retirement for people close to the current retirement age of 65 and for longterm unemployed aged over 60.
-- Unemployed to be allowed to work in health care, elderly care and child care with 90 percent of a regular salary, paid mostly by the government.

-- Small companies to be given support. Currently small companies pay five percent less in employment taxes on staff with total wages of less than 600,000 crowns and the government will propose to raise this to between 800,000 and 900,000 crowns.
-- 15,000 new university places to boost number of students.
-- Lower electricity taxes for power intensive industries.
-- Downscaling of plans for large cutbacks on dental care expenses.
-- No cutback on personal assistants for the disabled.
-- The government to allocate 1.1 billion crowns annually to expand Stockholm's traffic system.
-- Minimum wage to get sick leave to be raised to 8,000 crowns a month from 6,000 crowns.
